title: FurMark / Prime95 — Small FFTs: maximum heat
description: Small FFTs keep the transform inside the CPU caches, which produces the highest possible power draw and temperature — the famous 'power virus' workload. If the cooler survives an hour of small FFTs, it survives anything.

title: FurMark / Prime95 — Blend: CPU plus RAM
description: Blend alternates FFT sizes so the workload spills into system RAM, testing the CPU, memory controller, and DIMMs as one chain. A machine that passes small FFTs but fails Blend usually has a RAM problem, not a CPU problem.

title: FurMark / Prime95 — Lucas-Lehmer: the real Prime95 math
description: Prime95 proves Mersenne primes with the Lucas-Lehmer test: start s at 4, repeat s = s² − 2 modulo (2^p − 1) for p−2 rounds, and the number is prime only if s ends at zero. This demo runs the genuine algorithm on the exponent 19, proving 524287 prime.

title: FurMark / Prime95 — Reading the graphs

t: Safety rules and the full workflow
title: FurMark / Prime95 — Safety rules and the full workflow
description: Stress testing is safe when you respect heat: watch temperatures the whole time, stop at 90 C on the CPU or 85 C sustained on the GPU, and never leave a first-time overclock unattended. The full ritual is FurMark alone, Prime95 small FFTs, Prime95 Blend, then both together for the PSU — an hour each for a machine you trust.
